scene: Quiet Austin patio breakfast. In the foreground Neet turns his back to the wooden neighbor fence to sniff a single small acorn on the grass, posture calm and relaxed, all four fine legs clearly supporting real torso. Buddy, a few feet behind Neet and near fence, has just decided to answer the barking: stands long-bodied with mouth open toward fence, forefeet grounded, ears naturally hanging. Two distant golden-retriever heads appear above fence, Martha and Sally, but keep them minor and naturally supported as neighbors beyond fence, not disembodied heads floating in air (chest tops visible over low section). A patio table far to side carries coffee/smoothie/toast, no humans required. The joke is calm General refusing the noise while supposedly sensible Buddy cracks. No acorn in mouth, no eating. Neet ear roots natural, nub tiny. No text.
placement_after: Buddy’s eyes widened. “Wait— are we… not barking?” The Bark Sisters were still howling like sirens. He glanced at the quiet Neet, then at the fence. Someone had to answer. “Nope. Sorry. I’m going in.” And off he went, barking his best counter-attack.
alt_text: Neet quietly inspects an acorn while Buddy takes on the neighbors’ barking.
